### Summary

The hydro operator is one long function that turns the conserved state of a block into the increment of one
stage. It is organised in eight numbered sections, from the primitive conversion through the implicit correction to
the $x_1$ mass-flux sources, and every physics chapter of the book describes one piece of it. This section is the index
of those eight sections, so a reader can find where a scheme runs and what it hands to the next piece.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: primitives, $x_1$ flux, lateral states and fluxes, divergence, forcing, implicit, $x_1$ mass flux.

**Data.** In: `hydro_u` with fresh ghosts and the stage index. Out: a time-integrated increment, not a new state.

**Placement.** Once per stage, from the `advance` op (`stage_advance`); the sections run in the fixed order above.

**Activation.** The `dynamics:` card and the switches of @sec-ch12; each piece is owned by its chapter.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; the implicit step is stage-weighted only for an integrator of three or more stages.

**Evidence.** No dedicated test of the whole pipeline (missing evidence); each section cites its own tests.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) runs these in order.

1. The primitive conversion with the EOS and the solid marking (@sec-ch02, @sec-ch14-solids).
2. The $x_1$ face states, the well-balanced reference and wall treatment (@sec-ch05, @sec-ch14-wb). Then the
   $x_1$ Riemann flux (@sec-ch04), the sedimentation flux (@sec-ch08-sed) and the single-valued $x_1$ seam flux:
   on every internal $x_1$ seam, process or same-process, the register sets both sides to their mean
   (@sec-ch03-x1seams).
3. The lateral face states, with the cross-panel exchange of the cubed sphere (@sec-ch03).
4. The lateral fluxes with the face-flux covariance (@sec-ch04-fluxcov) and the tracer positivity limiter with its raw
   donor-factor exchange (@sec-ch08).
5. The flux divergence with the geometric sources (@sec-ch04).
6. The forcing and the face gravity work (@sec-ch07, @sec-ch06).
7. The implicit correction (@sec-ch09). Its time step is the stage weight times $\Delta t$ for an integrator of
   three or more stages (`rk3`, `rk3s4`) and $\Delta t$ for `rk1` and `rk2`, with a one-time warning when the caller never published a stage.
8. The $x_1$ mass-flux sources: the Coriolis and metric terms that read $\rho w$ take it from the stage's final
   $x_1$ face mass transfers, after the implicit correction (@sec-ch07).

Each section posts the face fluxes it forms to the block's flux register, which keeps the stage's totals and the
step's sums (@eq-ch01-stage-weight). Communication happens inside this pipeline as well as in the stage-entry exchange. The $x_1$ seam fluxes, the panel states
and the donor factors are synchronized at their own use sites. Disabled directions and unresolved dimensions are gated
separately. Orders and wall closures are derived by the owning chapters.

@fig-ch01-hydro-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-hydro-flow
#| fig-cap: "Follow the hydro increment through eight sections. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: EOS; x1 flux / seam; horizontal LR / panel; flux / donor factors; divergence / geometry; forcing / gravity; implicit increment; x1 mass-flux sources."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_hydro_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the eight sections are in this order.** Each section consumes what the one before it produced.

1. The primitives come first because every later section reads $\mathbf W$[^rg-76c144a0867d], and the solid marking must be in
   $\mathbf W$ before any reconstruction ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. The $x_1$ flux comes before the lateral ones because the lateral covariance of @sec-ch04-fluxcov reads the $x_1$
   differences of the face states. The seam rows must already be single-valued.
3. The positivity limiter runs after all three fluxes, because it scales the fluxes it has seen.
4. The divergence, the forcing and the gravity work follow, because they are sources on the stage increment. The
   implicit correction comes after them, because it acts on the assembled explicit increment, and the $x_1$
   mass-flux sources come last, because they read the $x_1$ mass transfers the implicit correction finalizes.

: Implementation anchors for the hydro pipeline. {#tbl-ch01-hydro-code}

1. Sections (1) and (2): primitives, the $x_1$ states, flux and seam ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. Sections (3) and (4): lateral states, lateral fluxes, the covariance and the limiter
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
3. Sections (5) to (8): divergence, forcing and gravity work, the implicit correction with `dt_corr`, and the
   $x_1$ mass-flux sources ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** The `dynamics` block selects the pieces; the keys accepted at this level are
`equation-of-state`, `reconstruct`[^rg-af5f86077ee8], `riemann-solver`, `verbose`, `disable-flux-x1`[^rg-ae041ae1bceb], `disable-flux-x2`[^rg-80c2fa91bc52],
`disable-flux-x3`[^rg-7e9816437e3b], `wb-wall-clamp`[^rg-008bc3db0d40], `conversion-order`[^rg-a68ffe8ce68d] (the order of the
$x_1$ cell-average to point conversion of the primitives, @sec-ch04-conv4), `anomaly`, `flux-covariance`,
`x1-mass-covariance`, `perturbation-flux`, `precision` and `conserve-axial-momentum`
({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}, read by {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `vertical`[^rg-febc4357099f], `horizontal`[^rg-9f229b714348].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-gas}
  reconstruct:
    vertical: {type: weno5}
    horizontal: {type: plm}
  riemann-solver: {type: lmars}
  wb-wall-clamp: true
```

Refused: any other key at this level, with its path in the error; the sub-block keys are listed with their
defaults in @sec-ch12-yaml. The hydro call itself is `phydro->forward(dt, hydro_u, vars)` from `stage_advance`,
and a direct caller that does not publish `rk_stage` first gets the one-time warning described in Limits.

of the pipeline cites its own tests in its chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The implicit time step is stage-weighted only for an integrator with three or more stages. A direct hydro caller
that has not published a valid stage receives a one-time warning and uses the full time step. Neither case is
measured here.
:::

[^rg-7e9816437e3b]: disable-flux-x3 — whether the third-coordinate flux is disabled

[^rg-008bc3db0d40]: wb-wall-clamp — whether to clamp the well-balanced wall continuation

[^rg-a68ffe8ce68d]: conversion-order — order of the $x_1$ cell-average to point conversion of the primitives: 2 (default) or 4

[^rg-febc4357099f]: vertical — options for the vertical reconstruction
